purpose: First-quarter wave slice for the fourteenth Ruleset Card — the §1.4 CI / build-farm card 'Green Light' / 'Untrusted Code, By Design', the first card founded on a §1.4 card and the first founded on a verb whose door mechanics shipped BEFORE the card (PlayerVerb.ReclaimNode @c8b92a2): 'Verb: isolate, expire, reclaim.' (:2686 verbatim) with Reclaim the blessed third word (owner ruling 2026-10-17, ADR-0017 #1; isolate stays dbaas's, expire stays a law) (14 of the 20-type launch canon, OD-14(a)). Slice shape mirrors the thirteen shipped g1 siblings: a reconnaissance opening on the calmest wall in the game, a peak built from the card's two structural pressures (runners held past their jobs and the desk flooding as the wall flushes), a trough where the enemy is the dead weekend eating the warmth budget while free-tier miners mine in the quiet, a surprise-with-composition wave carrying the line's named supply-chain threat — the fork-PR build running attacker code — landing beside the upstream rate-limit day, and a finale built on the card's own catastrophe: the boss beat with no registry id, a secret crossing a tenant boundary while every square on the most instantly readable board in the game stays green. Deliberately RULES-FREE (no rules block): §2.24 rule-carrier values stay in the g1 slices until the batch-D rule-adapter pass reads them for cross-type tables.

baseline._todo: §1.7: baseline continuous, diurnal, never zero. The rhythm name is authored from the card's own words (bundle tempo._todo carries the cites): 'Unit = a build minute / a job' (:2680) × 'engineering teams, who feel every second' (:2685) — the farm queues while the teams are awake and pushing, and the queue drains overnight but never empties: cron builds, badge refreshes, and dependency-cache warm-ups are this floor's idle hum. The card's dead-weekend claim ('a hard weekly shape and a dead weekend', :2694) is a SEASONALITY debt the never-zero baseline law keeps OUT of this curve — the waves lane owns curves, the numbers are the catalogue's (PROVISIONAL-B), and the weekend collapse lives in mechanics + the w3 trough's framing instead of a forged dip. neverZero holds in this line's register precisely because the card says the idle is the expensive part: the runners stay warm whether the queue is deep or empty, 'pure overhead you can't bill for' (:2683).

waves.title: key.wave.1
waves.note: Rule (b) honoured: first wave of any level ALWAYS <=40% of par (§1.7). The quarter opens on the wall half-lit: overnight queues drained, warm caches humming, green squares settling into their rows — and the only weather is a scanner's drizzle at the edge of the fleet, slow probes reading the public badge board, learning which repos are busy and which runners are reused (:2681's cold-averse reconnaissance; the Stealth debut, data-integrity front only). The opening teaches the board before it tests the boundary: 'the most instantly readable board in the game, and it's real' (:2704 verbatim) — every square answers, the queue is shallow, and the player learns to read green. The tension sits where the card puts it, in the dial's two ends: 'reused is fast and a cross-tenant contamination vector; ephemeral is safe and cold' (:2691-2692) — and today, nothing has asked which end the player chose.

waves.title: key.wave.2
waves.note: Rising floor beat one — the Monday Morning Wall lands, and it is the line's two native crowds arriving together. Two-Front (§2.24): jobs that will not release their runners (Sapper — the sipper re-worn: a session-shaped hold on a slot the fleet already billed away, 'a runner must be destroyed and rebuilt between jobs, which is pure overhead you can't bill for' :2682-2683 wearing the attacker's manners) spending concurrency on holds that are individually unremarkable, while the desk begins its climb (Swarm — the hydra of the queued quarter, every team asking 'is it my build or your farm?' as the wall flushes amber, 'developers tolerate slow builds and not queued builds' :2689-2690 verbatim) spending hands on tickets whose only honest answer is queue depth and an ephemeral-pool purchase. Two tenants of one Monday, two instruments, one lesson of wave two: the queue is the product, and the value of every crate in it is bleeding at a constant rate while it waits — 'patient, but value decays with queue time' (:11975 verbatim), the engine's value-decay law wearing this floor as its first card-named face.
waves.entropyNote: entropy budget here = f(estate age x size x (1 - maintenance spend)), NOT wave number (§2.24) — on this line maintenance spend IS the destroyer and the scrubber: 'runner-destroyer' and 'secret-scrubber' are this level's own counter list for its signature failures (bundle threats.unlockedByBuildables), and the card prices the unspent version in its fatal: runners that outlive their jobs are secrets that outlive their tenants (:2684).

waves.title: key.wave.3
waves.note: Rule (c): 30% is 50% below the preceding peak (60%) — >=45% satisfied. Dips are where the player builds (§1.7): the cache vault, the retention GC, the fork guard and the flakiness desk all get their window in the dead weekend. But the weekend is not empty, it is REASSIGNED: 'a hard weekly shape and a dead weekend' (:2694) means the engineering teams left and the free tier stayed — cryptominers in reused runners (Mimic — the griefer re-worn: a build that compiles nothing and earns everything, ':2698's dominant real abuse wearing a green square) spending data-integrity one idle runner at a time, while the big monorepo's nightly cache job settles onto the shared drum (Parasite — 'a customer whose monorepo needs 400GB of RAM' :2701 verbatim, the hoarder re-worn from inode appetite to cache appetite). Two fronts: data-integrity x reputation — contamination nobody sees while the hygiene percentage nobody watches slides, and the trough's real cost is written in the signature meter no engine can yet bind: 'genuinely fresh vs "reused because we were busy"' (:2702-2703).
waves.note2: the trough is also the reclaim beat's quiet setup: the empty weekend is the ONLY window when destroy-everything is affordable — the ephemeral posture is 'safe and cold' (:2692) and today, cold is cheap; the player who reclaims the fleet over the weekend arrives at Monday clean, and the engine's reclaim book (PlayerVerb.ReclaimNode @c8b92a2) is the furniture that makes the lesson purchasable.

waves.title: key.wave.4
waves.note: Compound-wave exemplar, farm variant: the stranger's code and the stranger's calendar land together — a merged PR carries attacker code that runs WITH the runner's borrowed production credentials (Bypass/Flyer debuts here, the every-4th-wave NEW ROLE beat, unseen in waves 1-3 — vulnerable-plugin-compromise re-worn from plugin marketplaces onto 'a fork-PR build that runs attacker code with your secrets', :2699 verbatim, the card's Interacts-with leg to '§2.5 supply chain' :2707 made playable), while the upstream package registry rate-limits every concurrent fetch at once (Splitter debuts too — mod-update-day re-framed onto 'the upstream API rate limit that stalls every build at once' :2701 verbatim, the dependency's calendar gate and the queue's fork in the same hour). Two fronts: concurrency (builds waiting on fetches hold their runners holding nothing) x data-integrity (the poisoned cache seeds every later build — 'cache poisoning between builds' :2700 verbatim). secondIncident inside the same window because on this line every supply is two supplies: the artifact that lied and the registry that would not answer.
waves.secondIncident: the rate-limit stall finds the poisoned build mid-propagation -> 1.8x multiplier applies (stated openly in the Codex, §2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.5
waves.note: The finale is the card's thesis completed — 'You sell the execution of arbitrary code written by strangers. That is not a bug in the product; it is the product.' (:2678-2679 verbatim) — and it arrives as one loud failure covering one quiet one: a grudge build forks until its host dies (Siege — the booter re-worn: ':2699's fork-until-the-host-dies, the registry's destruction shape told consequence-only per §9.11, the wall flushing red from the blast outward, 'the wall going red left-to-right as a bad dependency propagates' :2705 verbatim core) while a free-tier job reaches sideways through the warm-runner seam into another tenant's cache and out (Mimic — :2700's exfiltration, the leak the honest board cannot print: every square it reports is true, and the fatal square never turns :2684-2685). Hard wave draws TWO fronts — concurrency x data-integrity — per §2.24: the fleet's held slots and the boundary the slots share. The boss has no registry id and none is forged; the envelope event carries it (bundle threats._todo proposal). Win check: the wall flushed and refilled green, the hygiene stayed published, no secret crossed a tenant line, and the player proves they own the tension by choosing COLD when cold is what safety costs — reclaim the runners, eat the cold start, keep the strangers' secrets strangers.
waves.triageWindow: after any catastrophic failure in this wave: arrivals queue visibly outside, patience draining, hands freed 30s (§1.7).
